q: A plant cell placed in a hypertonic solution plasmolyses because water moves
opts: From the vacuole to the external solution by osmosis
Into the cell by active transport
From the cytoplasm to the nucleus
explain: Water moves out of the vacuole by osmosis to the more concentrated external solution, causing plasmolysis.

q: Which of the following is a correct sequence in the Calvin cycle?
explain: CO2 is first fixed by carboxylation, then reduced, then RuBP is regenerated.

q: A test cross of an organism with unknown genotype is performed by crossing it with a
explain: A test cross uses a homozygous recessive to reveal the unknown genotype.

q: The hormone that promotes stomatal closure during water stress is
explain: Abscisic acid causes stomatal closure to reduce transpiration.

q: Which nitrogenous base is found in RNA but not in DNA?
explain: Uracil replaces thymine in RNA.

q: The structure that prevents the collapse of the trachea during breathing is
explain: C-shaped cartilage keeps the trachea open.

q: In the nephron, glucose is normally completely reabsorbed in the
explain: All glucose is reabsorbed in the proximal convoluted tubule.

q: A colour-blind man marries a normal woman whose father was colour-blind. The probability that their son is colour-blind is
explain: The mother is a carrier, so 50% of sons receive the affected X.

q: The primary site of photosynthesis in a C4 plant like maize is the
explain: In C4 plants, the Calvin cycle occurs mainly in bundle sheath cells.

q: Which of the following is an example of convergent evolution?
explain: Dolphin and shark fins evolved separately for swimming, not from a common finned ancestor.

q: The enzyme that unwinds DNA during replication is
explain: Helicase breaks hydrogen bonds and unwinds the double helix.

q: Loss of the myelin sheath in a neurone will
explain: Myelin allows saltatory conduction; loss slows conduction.

q: In ecological succession, the pioneer species on a bare rock is most likely to be
explain: Lichens can colonise bare rock and start soil formation.

q: Which of the following blood vessels carries oxygenated blood at the lowest pressure?
explain: Pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood to the heart at low pressure.

q: The anticodon of a tRNA that carries methionine, if the mRNA codon is AUG, is
explain: Anticodon is complementary and antiparallel: AUG pairs with UAC.

q: A plant with genotype AaBb self-fertilizes. The proportion of offspring that are aabb is
explain: For a dihybrid self, aabb = 1/4 x 1/4 = 1/16.

q: The Bowman capsule is part of the
explain: Bowman capsule plus glomerulus forms the renal corpuscle of the nephron.

q: Which process releases the most ATP per glucose molecule?
explain: Aerobic respiration yields about 36-38 ATP, far more than glycolysis or fermentation.

q: The vestigial structure in humans that suggests a herbivorous ancestry is the
explain: Appendix is a remnant of a larger caecum used in cellulose digestion.

q: A person with blood group AB is called a universal recipient because
explain: AB blood has A and B antigens but no anti-A or anti-B antibodies.

q: In an ecosystem, the trophic level with the least energy is the
explain: Energy decreases at each transfer, so top consumers have least energy.

q: The hormone secreted by the alpha cells of the islets of Langerhans is
explain: Alpha cells secrete glucagon; beta cells secrete insulin.

q: Which of the following is NOT a function of the liver?
explain: Insulin is produced by the pancreas, not the liver.

q: The point at which the chromatids are attached in a chromosome is the
explain: Centromere joins sister chromatids.

q: If a DNA molecule has 30% adenine, the percentage of guanine is
The stage of mitosis where chromosomes align at the equator is
explain: Metaphase is alignment at the metaphase plate.

q: Which organism is a chemoautotroph?
explain: Nitrosomonas obtains energy from oxidation of ammonia, not light.

q: The opening and closing of stomata is mainly controlled by changes in the
explain: Turgor changes in guard cells open and close the pore.

q: A frameshift mutation is most likely caused by
explain: Deletion of one base shifts the reading frame for all subsequent codons.

q: The main excretory product of a freshwater fish is
explain: Freshwater fish are ammonotelic, excreting toxic ammonia directly into water.

q: Which of the following shows discontinuous variation?
explain: Blood group is discrete with no intermediates, controlled by few genes.

q: The structure that connects the foetus to the placenta is the
explain: Umbilical cord contains vessels linking foetus and placenta.

q: In the carbon cycle, the process that returns carbon dioxide to the atmosphere from dead organisms is
explain: Decomposers respire, releasing CO2 during decomposition.

q: The part of the brain that controls balance and coordination is the
explain: Cerebellum coordinates movement and balance.

q: Which of the following is a correct pair of antagonistic hormones?
explain: Insulin lowers blood sugar, glucagon raises it.

q: The number of chromosomes in a human secondary oocyte is
explain: After meiosis I, the secondary oocyte is haploid with 23 chromosomes, each double.

q: A student observes a cell with a large central vacuole, chloroplasts and a cell wall. The cell is most likely from a
explain: That combination is characteristic of plant cells.

q: Which of the following is the best definition of a niche?
opts: The role of an organism in its habitat
The number of organisms in a habitat
explain: Niche is the functional role, not just the place.

q: The enzyme pepsin works best at pH
explain: Pepsin is active in the acidic stomach.

q: During inspiration, the diaphragm
explain: Contraction flattens the diaphragm, increasing thoracic volume.

q: A population of rabbits is preyed on by foxes. If foxes are removed, the rabbit population will initially
explain: Removal of the predator removes a limiting factor, allowing rapid growth.

q: The genetic code is described as degenerate because
opts: More than one codon can code for the same amino acid
It has start and stop codons
explain: Degeneracy means multiple codons specify the same amino acid.

q: Which of the following is a C3 plant adaptation to reduce photorespiration?

This question is intentionally tricky. For JAMB, remember Kranz anatomy belongs to C4 plants.

q: The water potential of pure water at standard temperature and pressure is
explain: Pure water is the reference, defined as 0 MPa.

q: Which of the following is the first step in the germination of a seed?
explain: Imbibition - uptake of water - activates metabolism before division.

q: A child has sickle cell anaemia. The genotype of the child is
explain: Sickle cell anaemia is homozygous recessive HbS HbS.

q: The loop of Henle is mainly concerned with
opts: Reabsorption of water and salts to create a gradient
explain: The loop creates the medullary osmotic gradient for water reabsorption.

q: Which of the following is an example of mutualism?
explain: Lichen is algae + fungus both benefiting.
